title: COVID-19 Pandemic
description: Beginning in late 2019 and escalating globally through 2020, COVID-19 forced governments to make simultaneous public-health and macroeconomic decisions under extreme uncertainty. Policymakers had to balance mobility restrictions, testing and treatment capacity, fiscal support, and vaccine strategy while preserving social trust and institutional legitimacy.

dr_elena.name: Dr. Elena
dr_elena.role: Senior Economist, Monetary Policy & Financial Stability Division
dr_elena.motivation: Protect economic stability while supporting the public health response
dr_elena.opening_scene: Dr. Elena reviews incoming alerts from WHO headquarters. Cluster outbreaks are appearing across East Asia — 282 confirmed cases in Thailand, Japan, and South Korea. Her background in systemic risk gives her a framework, but this threat spans health systems, supply chains, and fiscal capacity simultaneously. Every decision in the next weeks will define the trajectory.

questions.text: First cases of novel COVID-19 appear in Thailand, Japan and South Korea, totalling 282 confirmed cases of COVID-19.
questions.fun_fact: On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a global pandemic.

options.text: Focus on prioritizing the procurement of personal protective equipment.
options.feedback: Population is split in reaction to your decision: while some appreciate the maintenance of normalcy and practical solutions, many are beginning to lose faith in disease control and are having doubts about governance ability. First results of COVID's arrival are devastating, with a high initial death toll causing mass panic. Tread carefully with your next choices.

options.text: Cancel all travel outside of country, and enact quarantine periods for recent travellers at lengths of 14 days, as per current research.
options.feedback: The population is reassured with harsh policy to stop disease spread, and is mostly concerned with population control, as opposed to the virus itself. The arrival of COVID was put off by harsh measures, however as COVID has now reached your borders (although later), government has been caught shorthanded in terms of research and reactive measures, causing for lower levels of preparedness.

options.text: Cancel all travel from Asia, and send top immunology officials to affected areas to better understand capabilities of the virus, while having a smaller focus on current measures like PPE.
options.feedback: The population is slightly reassured due to restricted travel freedoms, and is proud of the country's efforts on the preventative side, however some feel that focus should be shifted to reactionary measures. While COVID managed to reach your borders with relative ease, reports from the scientific front are positive, and show potential progress towards vaccination, which has secured your country with a pathway to access vaccination for a more affordable rate. Still, vaccine development is a long way away and is not helping protect health at the moment.

options.text: Cancel all travel from Asia, and begin procurement of testing infrastructure, while having a smaller focus on current measures like PPE.
options.feedback: The population is slightly reassured due to restricted travel freedoms, and has begun to accept the reality that the government believes COVID will reach local borders. While COVID managed to reach your borders with relative ease, the pragmatic decision to invest in testing infrastructure, as a primary target, has allowed for greater tracking of virality, while still considering reactionary measures to stop spread.

questions.text: As COVID reaches North America, plans must be made to slow the spread of the virus as transmission rates begin to take off!
questions.fun_fact: Non-pharmaceutical interventions were the primary response before vaccine deployment scaled globally.

options.text: Create optional distancing and masking guidelines, that are not enforced, maintaining free choice and elements of normalcy, allowing society to operate as per normal.
options.feedback: While normalcy has increased potential stability of the economy, and has increased the support of populations at lesser risk, figures report a comparably high rate of initial death, especially in long term care homes.

options.text: Maintain 14 day travel quarantines, and impose 14 day quarantines on those who have tested, or come into contact with the infected while encouraging distancing and masking guidelines.
options.feedback: This middle ground policy experiences a significant, but comparably average death toll, however a middle ground stance on distancing and masking creates a "weakest link" situation where the free operation of businesses and schools is jeopardized by free choice, causing potential economic disruption, and may potentially lead to larger, sweeping lockdowns.

options.text: Force societal isolation using digital surveillance, creating mass city wide lockdowns, eliminating normalcy.
options.feedback: While the spread of COVID has strongly decreased and many human lives have been saved, this decision puts you at odds with the wrath of frustrated and isolated protesters, and an economy in crisis.

options.text: Order the closing businesses and schools outside of essential services to help stop the spread of the virus, allowing free movement while enforcing mandatory distancing and masking guidelines eliminating normalcy.
options.feedback: While maintaining essential services, and closing schools and non-essential businesses, regulated freedom of movement minimizes backlash as commerce and education move online however the economy still enters a state of crisis.

questions.text: The effects of COVID 19 have worsened and are beginning to tighten their strain on global economies. How should we proceed?
questions.fun_fact: Global GDP contracted sharply in 2020 while emergency fiscal measures reached historic levels in many countries.

options.text: Subsidize businesses in recovery and entice investment and corporate spending through the offering of interest free loans and lower interest rates.
options.feedback: Government spending stays relatively under control, prioritizing the stability of big business, while relying on the incentive effect proves to provide less boost than comparative measures, taking the longest time for the economy to recover.

options.text: Enact targeted support for industries like tourism most affected by the pandemic, while subsidizing (through government) lower working hours to reduce the possible opportunities for spread.
options.feedback: Unemployment remains stable, as extremely few are laid off. As a result, bureaucracy is maintained for largely efficient operation. While many become infected due to the nature of reduced working hours, spending power is slightly improved under middle ground measures.

options.text: Introduce a significant fiscal stimulus focused on consumer, while increasing unemployment benefits, as well as the buying of bonds and Quantitative Easing.
options.feedback: This Keynesian fiscal policy creates an instantaneous rebound—but its effects are so vast, there are considerable implications of inflation and national debt.

options.text: Offer strong unemployment benefits that pay the majority of a working salary for furloughed workers, while subsidizing key industries affected by the pandemic, grant like benefits for the self employed as well as the buying of bonds and Quantitative Easing.
options.feedback: Unemployment remains reasonable, and the social safety net helps the laid off find work. Key industries see rebounds, however some businesses have become unsustainable as they rely on constant support.

questions.text: As Vaccination opportunities become available, how will your country distribute a potential cure?
questions.fun_fact: Leading vaccine candidates reported approximately 95% efficacy in late-stage 2020 trials.

options.text: Negotiate with vaccine developers, distributing vaccines earlier than most, but at a high cost to the patient.
options.feedback: Major issues of inequality, as many high risk populations cannot afford the price of vaccination, however many receive near instant access to protection.

options.text: Only distribute government funded vaccinations amongst the highest risk populations with the option for those outside of target populations to pay to receive vaccination.
options.feedback: Clear prioritization of at risk populations builds confidence to fight disease, with lower risk individuals with willingness and ability to pay also receiving treatment.

options.text: Subsidize free vaccination for all.
options.feedback: Vaccination is accessible, and a majority of individuals have been protected, however still spread continues across all demographics. Still, many believe this decision to represent the equilibrium of freedom and safety.

options.text: Subsidize mandated free vaccination for all.
options.feedback: Vaccination is accessible and mandated: the maximum extent of the vaccination's effect is experienced at the sacrifice of personal freedom.

questions.text: COVID, in many ways, seems to be here to stay for the next little while. How might we balance health, well being and economic well being to reach societal equilibrium once again?
questions.fun_fact: Many economies faced simultaneous goals: restoring mobility, sustaining growth, and preventing renewed health shocks.

options.text: Pull fiscal/monetary incentive supports from corporate businesses and lenders once the number of cases falls beneath a particular threshold.
options.feedback: Markets regain familiar structures, leaving many corporations vulnerable, but improving government depth and encouraging innovation through an incentive framework.

options.text: Re-open shuttered businesses and schools at the point of mass vaccination, should its results be effective.
options.feedback: Society largely returns to equilibrium, however mass vaccination does not guarantee against the emergence of further waves of disease.

options.text: Continue with current closure policy/encouraged precautions until the declared end of the pandemic.
options.feedback: While this approach ensures the safety of all humans involved, it jeopardizes the interests of business, and risks waiting for too long to act.

options.text: Once the amount of new cases falls beneath a particular threshold, and there is mass vaccination, and automatic stabilizers are maintained for the near future, precautions can begin to roll back.
options.feedback: Balancing spread rates and vaccination, while continuing economic support, helps communities best adapt to a new normal.

result_bands.title: Scenario 1: Fragile / Crisis Escalates
result_bands.summary: COVID cases continue to rise. Significantly higher death toll than comparable countries. Populations are undervaccinated. While lax regulations may have allowed for early term economic success, further viral growth jeopardizes economic prospects. Vaccination remains available to a shrinking minority.

result_bands.title: Scenario 2: Strained but Recoverable
result_bands.summary: Slightly above average death toll. Economy well adjusted to normalcy. Unemployment remains low. Treatments possibly hidden behind paywalls. Corporations prioritized over human impact.

result_bands.title: Scenario 3: Stable with Trade-offs
result_bands.summary: Mass vaccination achieved. Significant inflation achieved, with significant ramifications. Healthy business, propped up by fiscal support. Prioritization of human impact over economy and national debt.

result_bands.title: Scenario 4: Strong / Strategic Advantage
result_bands.summary: Mass Vaccination achieved. On track to eliminate viral threat. Relatively high employment. Institutions emerge more resilient due to selective government support. Cautious and Pragmatic approach balances proactive and reactive measures to support physical healing and economic policy.
